thread:
carmen: quick heads-up, staging runs show a latency/throughput regression after yesterday's kernel handoff for Llama2-13B int8 (AWQ). p95 up ~20% on batch>=6, long seqs >1024.
ben: ouch. is this after the new kernel_selector weights change?
car men: yep — kernel_selector v2 landed to prefer the "vec-packed" kernel for headkv dims>64. metric: saw p95 jump from 180ms -> 220ms on the same infra (A10s).
alice: can you paste the perf trace? small snippet is fine.
carmen: sending a short trace from perf-run (seq=1536, batch=8). trimmed: 
```
[timeline] tokengen: 0.00-0.18s
  kernel_vec_packed (call 1): 0.045s
  kernel_vec_packed (call 2): 0.047s
  kv_read (load from host): 0.082s
  fallback_kernel (call N): 0.023s
  total step: 0.220s
[notes] high % of time in repeated small memcpy + kernel dispatchs for heads/kv dims mismatch
```
ben: looks like more kernel flips + mem copies. could be headkv stride causing misaligned loads. did the selector try to pick vec-packed because heads*kv % 64 == 0?
david: I ran a microbench: for head_k=64, kv_dim=128 we see vec-packed wins for short seqs but breaks for long seqs due to extra KV load passes. results: 
```
batch=1 seq=128 p95(vec)=85ms p95(dot)=92ms
batch=8 seq=1536 p95(vec)=220ms p95(dot)=182ms
```
eva: interesting. maybe the kernel cost model doesn't account for KV-cache eviction churn at higher batch * seq. selector's cost_estimator uses perf table from short seq runs only.
perf-bot: perf-regression alert created: https://perf.internal/reports/1765559999 - attaching flamegraph and kernel switch log.
alice: two quick experiments: 1) force kernel_selector to prefer "dot-unified" for head_k<=64; 2) increase batch_affinity window to keep KV cached per microbatch. which do we try first?\carmen: let's try (1) first — it's low-risk, quick rollback. I can build a canary patch and run against staging batch sweep.
ben: also add an instrumentation counter: kernel_switch_count per inference. if we spike above N, fallback to safer kernel.
david: agree. i'll add counter + cheap hysteresis (if kernel_switch_count > 3 within step -> pin kernel).
eva: for longer term, we should expand the estimator table with seq distribution buckets and add a KV-eviction penalty term. also run AWQ-calib-vs-gptq sampling to ensure accuracy isn't impacted by the fallback.
car men: note on accuracy: AWQ int8 outputs matched fp16 within eval tolerance on our sample suite. fallback will not change quant tables.
ben: timeline? Carmen, can you run the canary tonight and drop results by EOD?
carmen: yep doing sweep at 2100 PST. i'll post summary + installer link.
perf-bot: canary run scheduled: job/1765559999-canary-1 - ETA 40m
alice: thanks all. small follow-up: add to the rollout doc a step to abort if p95 increases >10% for batch>=4. we keep failing early otherwise. :warning:
car men: noted and added to deploy checklist.
ben: good find — probably an estimator edge case. once canary confirms, we'll ship a patch to kernel_selector and keep the hysteresis counter for 2 weeks. :thumbsup:
